extracted.subtask_description: A specimen/catalog of typefaces, sizes, styles, and special glyphs showing how sample text and characters render across families, point sizes, weights, scripts, and decorative/display sizes. Used as a reference when selecting faces and verifying glyph support for book and print composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-size (body and display sizes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point sizes are shown explicitly (six point, eight point, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, fourteen, sixteen, eighteen, twenty, twenty-two, twenty-four, twenty-eight, thirty, thirty-two, thirty-six, forty, forty-four, forty-eight, sixty, etc.), with the same sample text set at each size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specimens to evaluate legibility and appearance at each point size; compare how the same text looks at body sizes (6–12 pt) versus display/headline sizes (18–60 pt). Examples: 'When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius...' shown at many point sizes to judge reading size and headline impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface family selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple named type families are presented (e.g., Scotch Roman, Bookman Old Style, Monotype, Antique Greek, Caslon Old Style, No. 8 Old Style, Elzevir Italic, Condensed Old Style, Extended Old Style, French Old Style, Cheltenham, Cheltenham Wide, Cheltenham Condensed, Cheltenham Bold, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a face by examining the specimen pages to judge overall tone, proportion, and suitability for body text versus display use. The catalog shows each family in variants and multiple sizes so designers can choose families appropriate to the book's voice and intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight and style variations (bold, italic, condensed, extended, wide)
rubrics_metrics.description: For many families the specimen shows style and weight variants such as italic, bold, condensed, extra condensed, bold condensed, wide, extended, and bold extra condensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare weights and styles within a family to decide emphasis strategy (e.g., italics for emphasis, bold for headings) and to ensure consistent optical color across weights. The specimens provide side-by-side visual examples at multiple sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading / line-spacing indication (Leaded vs Solid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some specimens are labeled '[Leaded]' or '[Solid]', indicating different line spacing or setting methods used in the sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these markers to evaluate the effect of added leading versus solid (no added leading) on readability and texture of text blocks; helps set appropriate interline spacing when composing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script and multilingual glyph support
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include multiple scripts with examples: Monotype/Antique/Inscription Greek, Hebrew, Nestorian Syriac, Arabic, Ethiopic, and other inscription forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check these pages to verify the chosen face provides required language/script support and to evaluate the visual compatibility of non-Latin scripts with Latin text when setting multilingual material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and miscellaneous signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets of punctuation, mathematical signs, and miscellaneous symbols are shown (e.g., = + − × < > ± : :: / % ° ' " # § © ® etc.) across sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect these samples to ensure glyph shapes, alignment, and optical weight of symbols match the typeface and remain legible at intended sizes; confirm presence of necessary symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior and inferior letters and figures (superscripts/subscripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections labeled 'MONOTYPE SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR LETTERS AND FIGURES' and similar show superscript (superior) and subscript (inferior) forms and how numerals and letters appear in those positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these specimens to confirm the availability and readability of superior/inferior glyphs for footnotes, ordinal indicators, chemical formulas, and citations; check proportion at body sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled letters and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry 'CANCELED LETTERS AND FIGURES' displays how canceled or struck-through letters/figures render at specific sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference this to see the legibility and aesthetic of canceled glyph treatment (useful for proofing, editorial marks, or design effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotype vs Foundry/Manufacturing distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens are organized under headings such as 'MONOTYPE' and also show other foundry families; some captions indicate monotype-specific cut/style differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that different manufacturing systems (Monotype casting vs other foundries) produce subtle design and metric differences; consult the monotype pages when matching machine-set type or when requiring machine-set numerals/spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display / headline typography (large caps and all-caps display)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large display sizes and all-caps specimens are provided (e.g., 'THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT...' in varying large point sizes), and special display cuts (e.g., condensed bold extra condensed) are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use display samples to judge optical spacing, kerning, and impact for titles and headings; check how uppercase settings perform at very large sizes and whether tracking/kerning adjustments are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented letters and diacritics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections titled 'ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT' and 'SPECIAL CHARACTERS — ALL SIZES' show accented Latin letters and diacritics at small text sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate the presence and clarity of diacritics and accented glyphs at body text sizes (6–12 pt) to ensure readability and correct composition of languages requiring accents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inscription and decorative letterforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples labeled 'INSCRIPTION GREEK' and decorative uppercase inscription-like specimens are included to show carved/inscriptional styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to these when selecting or designing display inscriptions, dedications, or decorative headings where a carved or monumental appearance is desired; check for legibility at intended sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeral styles and figure sets (old-style, lining, tabular, proportional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerals in various forms and groupings are shown (e.g., sequences '1234567890', '123456-890', superior/inferior numerals, old-style figures in text, and variants across point sizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the numeral specimens to choose between old-style (text) figures and lining figures for body text, to verify tabular alignment, and to ensure numeric color and size match surrounding text.
